slowest_experiments.description: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Live model inference over full GSM8K corpus with two model variants. Each forward pass requires loading, tokenizing, and running inference on 1319 questions per model. No batching ceiling — ran to completion without timeout gate.

slowest_experiments.description: JEPA fast-path gate integration (checkpoint: tests failing)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Test suite failure mid-experiment forced a conductor checkpoint rather than clean completion. The integration touched multiple pipeline layers; failing tests likely caused repeated re-runs of slow JEPA training loops trying to get green. Checkpoint overhead + retry cycles compound.

slowest_experiments.description: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: 3B parameter model (vs. 0.8B baseline) requires ~3.75x more VRAM and ~3.75x more inference time per question. No model-size timeout scaling — same fixed budget as smaller experiments. GPU contention likely extended wall time further.

slowest_experiments.description: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Typed IR constraint evaluation requires Z3 solver calls per question on top of LLM inference, creating a two-stage per-sample latency. Z3 calls are CPU-bound and not GPU-parallelizable, so GPU and CPU bottlenecked sequentially.

slowest_experiments.description: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Full training run — not just inference. Multi-domain dataset assembly plus training loop over multiple epochs. No early-stopping or checkpoint-and-resume strategy; single monolithic run. Training is inherently longer than inference.

gpu_state_at_retro.assessment: Both GPUs at 98% VRAM occupancy with 0% compute utilization. This is a textbook zombie-process state: models loaded into VRAM but not computing. Any new experiment requiring >500MB VRAM will fail to allocate and fall back to CPU or block.

bottlenecks_identified: GPU VRAM monopolization by zombie processes: 98% of both RTX 3090s' VRAM is held by idle processes (0% utilization). New experiments cannot get GPU slots, forcing CPU fallback or blocks. 7 of 12 tracked processes have wall times >4 hours with negligible CPU activity.

No model caching or reuse between experiments: Each live benchmark experiment re-loads model weights from disk (3-15GB), consuming 30-90 seconds of wall time before first inference token. With 374 experiments, cumulative model-load overhead is substantial.

Sequential experiment execution: All 374 experiments ran sequentially. The two RTX 3090s were never exploited for parallel experiment execution. Independent experiments (different model sizes, different domains) could have run concurrently.

Test failure forcing checkpoint-and-retry cycles: Exp 308 burned 105 minutes because test failures mid-experiment triggered conductor checkpoints and partial reruns. A pre-flight test gate (run affected tests before starting the experiment script) would catch this at minute 2 not minute 60.

Flat timeout budget for all experiment categories: Benchmark experiments (live model inference over 1000+ questions) have fundamentally different runtime profiles than unit experiments. The same 45-minute watchdog that is appropriate for a unit experiment kills a legitimate benchmark before it can complete.

Z3 solver calls not parallelized with GPU inference: In Exp 221 and similar typed-IR experiments, Z3 constraint checking and LLM inference run sequentially per sample. These are independent per question and could run in parallel via asyncio or a thread pool.

Doc reconciliation happening synchronously within experiment turns: ops/changelog.md, ops/status.md, _bmad/traceability.md, and openspec spec updates run inside the same conductor turn as the implementation. On slow experiments this adds 5-10 minutes of non-compute overhead to an already-long turn.

No pre-experiment GPU health gate for large-model experiments: Exp 184 (3B model) ran without verifying available VRAM headroom first. If zombies are holding VRAM, the experiment discovers this only after the model fails to load, wasting the turn startup cost.
improvements_suggested: Implement a GPU zombie reaper: Add a conductor pre-flight step that runs `gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies` before any live GPU experiment. Processes idle >30 minutes holding >500MB VRAM are killed and VRAM is freed. This alone unlocks ~46GB VRAM currently inaccessible.

Introduce experiment tier classes with tier-specific timeout budgets: UNIT (10 min), SCAFFOLD (20 min), BENCHMARK_SMALL (60 min), BENCHMARK_LARGE (120 min), TRAINING (180 min). The conductor sets ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog budget from the tier, not a single flat value.

Run independent experiments in parallel across the two GPUs: Use a two-slot conductor queue. Experiments tagged `gpu_independent` (different models, different domains, no shared state) execute concurrently on GPU 0 and GPU 1, halving elapsed wall time for independent pairs.

Add a pre-flight test gate: Before executing the experiment script, run only the tests that cover the new experiment's module. If any fail, abort immediately (< 30 seconds) instead of running the full experiment and discovering failures mid-way.

Implement persistent model server for benchmark-class experiments: A long-lived vLLM or llama.cpp server holds model weights in VRAM across experiments. Benchmark experiments send HTTP requests rather than loading weights from scratch each time. Eliminates per-experiment load latency.

Parallelize Z3 + LLM inference with asyncio: For experiments combining solver calls and model inference (Exp 221 pattern), spawn Z3 checks and next-batch LLM inference concurrently. Per-question latency drops by the slower of the two, not their sum.

Defer doc reconciliation to an async post-experiment pass: Implementation and test execution run in the main conductor turn. ops/changelog.md, traceability.md, and spec updates run in a lightweight follow-up turn that does not block the next experiment from starting.

Add a VRAM headroom check before large-model experiments: Before any experiment that requires a model >2GB, run `gpu_monitor.py --json` and verify free_mb > model_size_mb * 1.2. If not, trigger zombie reaper first. Prevents the silent CPU fallback that distorts benchmark results.

Emit a 'not_run' artifact for experiments with scripts but no result JSON: The conductor should detect scripts matching `experiment_NNN_*.py` with no corresponding result file and write a minimal `{status: 'not_run'}` artifact. This surfaces silent drops like Exps 433/434/435 immediately.

time_savings_breakdown.gpu_zombie_reaper_frees_vram_prevents_cp: 8% — eliminates VRAM contention that forced ~30 experiments to CPU fallback, each adding ~15 min over GPU baseline
time_savings_breakdown.parallel_experiment_execution_dual_gpu: 12% — running independent experiment pairs in parallel on GPU 0 + GPU 1 halves wall time for ~25% of experiments
time_savings_breakdown.persistent_model_server_eliminates_load_: 6% — removes 30-90s model-load overhead from each of ~60 live benchmark experiments
time_savings_breakdown.tier_specific_timeout_prevents_unnecessa: 4% — benchmark experiments that were killed at 45 min and rerun later (RETRO-026 pattern) complete in one shot
time_savings_breakdown.preflight_test_gate_prevents_checkpoint_: 2% — catches test failures like Exp 308 in under 30s rather than burning 60-105 minutes before discovery

open_retro_items.description: GPU 1 scheduling reliability: experiments preferentially scheduled to GPU 0 even when GPU 1 is available, causing GPU 0 VRAM exhaustion while GPU 1 sits underutilized.
Benchmark-class experiments (Exps 427, 428, 429) require >45 min budget but are killed by current ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog flat cap. Tier-specific budgets not yet implemented.
Silent experiment drop: Exps 433, 434, 435 have scripts and passing tests but no result JSON. Conductor never executed them and emitted no artifact.

meta_reflection: This milestone demonstrates a systemic pattern: GPU resources are allocated at experiment start and never reclaimed. Over 374 experiments, this compounds into 98% VRAM occupancy by idle processes. The fix is architectural — the conductor must treat GPU memory as a managed resource with explicit acquire/release, not a fire-and-forget allocation. The estimated 32% time saving is conservative; if the persistent model server and parallel execution are both implemented, the compounding effect likely exceeds 40%.
